title.en: Sexual maturity rating and pubertal assessment

intro.en: Tanner staging of breast, genital and pubic hair development with pubertal timing and wrist bone age.

title.en: Female pubertal staging of breast and pubic hair

items.summary: Five stage rating of breast budding and pubic hair spread used to grade physical maturation in girls.

head: Stage
Hair character and spread
rows: Childhood pattern with no true pubic hair.
Sparse straight strands, lightly coloured, along the inner labial edge.
Darker hair that starts to curl and grows thicker.
Thick curly hair, plentiful yet still below adult quantity.
Adult triangular spread reaching the inner thigh surface.

head: Stage
Breast and areola appearance
rows: Childhood chest with no glandular budding.
Small raised bud of breast and nipple with a wider areola.
Whole breast and areola larger, with one smooth outline.
Nipple and areola stand out as a second mound above the breast.
Full adult contour where only the nipple projects.

viva.q: What marks the shift from stage 3 to stage 4 breast development?
viva.a: The nipple and areola lift into a secondary mound above the breast in stage 4, whereas stage 3 keeps a single smooth contour.

viva.q: How does stage 5 female pubic hair differ from stage 4?
viva.a: Stage 5 shows an adult triangular pattern spreading onto the inner thighs; stage 4 stays abundant but below adult amount and spread.

viva.q: A girl has a small breast bud with a widened areola. What stage is this?
viva.a: Stage 2, defined by elevation of breast and nipple into a small mound with increased areolar diameter.

title.en: Male pubertal staging of genitalia and pubic hair

items.summary: Five stage rating combining pubic hair texture, scrotal and testicular volume, and penile growth to grade maturation in boys.

head: Stage
Pubic hair
Scrotum and testicular volume
Penis
rows: Skin reddens and texture changes, volume 4-10 ml.
Darker hair that begins to curl, still scanty.
Near adult texture, coarse and curly, below adult amount.
Scrotum larger and darker, volume 15-20 ml.

blocks.title: Orchidometer
bullets: A string of graded beads is matched against each testis to read volume in ml.
The bead reading places the boy in the volume band of the stage table above.

viva.q: What testicular volumes separate the five male stages?
viva.a: Under 4 ml, then 4-10 ml, 10-15 ml, 15-20 ml, and above 20 ml from stage 1 through stage 5.

viva.q: How is an orchidometer used in staging?
viva.a: Graded beads are compared with each testis to read its volume in ml, and that volume fixes the genital stage.

viva.q: What penile change marks stage 4 over stage 3?
viva.a: Stage 3 mainly lengthens the shaft, while stage 4 adds breadth with enlargement of the glans.

title.en: Pubertal timing, sequence and wrist bone age

aka: Bone age from the wrist film
items.summary: Age cutoffs for late and early puberty, the usual order of secondary sexual characters, growth spurt stages, and reading bone age from wrist ossification centres.

blocks.title: Growth spurt stages
bullets: Boys usually show their fastest growth across stages 3 and 4.
Girls usually show their fastest growth across stages 1 and 2.

blocks.title: Usual order of secondary sexual characters
bullets: Girls follow breast budding, then pubic hair, then first periods.
Boys start with testicular enlargement, then pubic, underarm and facial hair in turn.
Penile enlargement with first seminal emission follows testicular growth in boys.

blocks.title: Late and early puberty cutoffs
bullets: Late puberty means no secondary sexual characters by 17 years in girls or 14 years in boys.
It also covers a girl with no periods by 16 years.
Early puberty means breast budding before 8 years or first periods before 10 years in girls.
It means any pubertal onset before 9.5 years in boys.

blocks.title: Bone age from a left wrist film under 8 years
bullets: Take a radiograph of the left wrist in children below 8 years.
Bone age in years equals the count of wrist ossification centres minus 1.
Read centres from thumb side to little finger side with this memory line: She looks too pretty, try to catch her.

head: Bone
Age in years when its centre appears

blocks.title: Points to remember
bullets: Daytime bladder control is expected after 4 years and night time dryness after 6 years; later wetting is termed enuresis.

viva.q: When is puberty called delayed and when precocious?
viva.a: Delayed means no secondary sexual characters by 17 years in girls or 14 in boys, or no periods by 16. Precocious means breast budding before 8, periods before 10, or any male pubertal onset before 9.5 years.

viva.q: How do you estimate bone age from a wrist film in a young child?
viva.a: Film the left wrist under 8 years, count the ossification centres, and subtract 1 to get the bone age in years.

viva.q: What is the usual sequence of female secondary sexual development?
viva.a: Breast budding first, then pubic hair, then first menstrual bleeding.

viva.q: At which stages does the growth spurt fall in each sex?
viva.a: Stages 3 and 4 in boys, stages 1 and 2 in girls.
